definitions.explanation: An underground passage, especially one built through a hill or under a road, river, or other obstacle.

examples.japanese: トンネルを{抜|ぬ}けると{海|うみ}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: When we emerged from the tunnel, we could see the ocean.
examples.notes: トンネルを抜ける = to pass through a tunnel

examples.japanese: この{山|やま}を{通|とお}るトンネルは5キロもある。
examples.english: The tunnel through this mountain is 5 kilometers long.

examples.japanese: トンネル{工事|こうじ}で{渋滞|じゅうたい}していた。
examples.english: There was traffic congestion due to tunnel construction.

notes:
FAMOUS LITERARY REFERENCE: The opening line of Kawabata Yasunari's novel "Snow Country" (雪国): 「{国境|くにざかい}の{長|なが}いトンネルを{抜|ぬ}けると{雪国|ゆきぐに}であった」(The train came out of the long tunnel into the snow country).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・トンネルを{抜|ぬ}ける (to pass through a tunnel)
・トンネル{工事|こうじ} (tunnel construction)
・{海底|かいてい}トンネル (undersea tunnel)
・{地下|ちか}トンネル (underground tunnel)
